<!-- All news items below this line -->{{Current events|year=2003|month=05|day=18|content=
* ''[[The Guardian]]'' reporter [[Andrew Meldrum]], the last foreign journalist in [[Zimbabwe]], is forcibly deported after covering the country for the last 23 years.
* In [[Belgium]] federal elections take place. The main winners are the social-democratic cartel [[Socialistische Partij Anders|Different Socialist Party]]–[[Spirit (political party)|Spirit]] and the extreme right wing [[Vlaams Blok]]. The biggest losses are for the green party [[Agalev]].
* A nationwide [[referendum]] on record nine issues takes place in [[Switzerland]]. Abolition of [[nuclear power]] is rejected. Reduction and modernization of army is approved. It ends requirement of nuclear [[bunker]] in every home and famous [[bicycle brigade]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/europe/3037503.stm | work=BBC News | first=Imogen | last=Foulkes | title=Switzerland's marathon vote | date=May 18, 2003}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swissinfo.org/sen/swissinfo.html?siteSect=105&sid=1865118 |title=Voters throw out nuclear ban - SWI swissinfo.ch |publisher=Swissinfo.org |date=2003-05-18 |accessdate=2015-10-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.asahi.com/international/update/0518/008.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2017-09-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060521194400/http://www.asahi.com/international/update/0518/008.html |archive-date=2006-05-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[Indonesia]]n president [[Megawati Sukarnoputri]] declares martial law in the breakaway republic of [[Aceh]] (→ [[2003–2004 Indonesian offensive in Aceh|Indonesian offensive in Aceh]]).
* In [[Slovakia]], voters approve a [[2003 Slovak European Union membership referendum|referendum on joining the European Union]].  The referendum is only advisory, the decision is in the hands of the national legislature, but it is expected to be approved.
